Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 5 January,
2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Srinivas
 Criminal Revision Case No.982 of 2009
Order:

entities.text: Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Assailing the judgment dated 18.06.2009 in Crl.A.No.48 of 2007 on the file of the Court of learned I Additional Sessions Judge, Nellore, confirming the conviction passed by the judgment dated 30.04.2007 in C.C.No.558 of 2002 on the file of the Court of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur, but modified and reduced the sentenced from six (6) months to three (3)
months, for the charge under Section 16(i)(a)(ii), 7(i) and 2(ia)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act read with Rule 23 and 29 of Food Adulteration Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"), the petitioners/accused filed the present criminal revision case under Section 397 r/w.401 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (hereinafter referred to as "Cr.P.C.").
2. The revision case was admitted on 22.06.2009 and the sentence of imprisonment imposed against the petitioner was suspended, vide orders in Crl.R.C.M.P.No.1326 of 2009.

3. The shorn of necessary facts are that:
i).
On 07.03.2002, P.W.1/A.Rameswaram, Food Inspector inspected the shop of petitioner at Allur Village and found sunflower oil was kept in open tin for sale.

Then,
he purchased 450 grams of sunflower oil, divided the same into three parts, filled the same in three clean, dry and empty bottles, sealed them as per procedure and sent one sample bottle to the Public Analyst, Hyderabad and deposited the remaining two sample bottles with the Local Health Authority and subsequently, he received report from the analyst stating that the sunflower oil contains cotton seed oil also, thereby it was adulterated.
ii).

Thereafter, he sent proposals to the Director, Institute of Preventive Medicine,
Hyderabad and obtained sanction orders to prosecute the petitioner and prepared complaint and filed the complaint before the Court of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. The said complaint was taken on file and numbered as C.C.No.558 of 2002 and before the trial Court, P.Ws.1 and 2, who are complainant and mediator, were examined and Exs.P.1 to P.23 were exhibited on behalf of the prosecution.
No oral and documentary evidence was adduced on behalf of the petitioner/accused.

5. After full pledged trial, the trial Court convicted the petitioner for the charge under Section 16(i)(a)(ii), 7(i) and 2(ia)(b) read with Rule 23 and 29 of the Act and sentenced him to under Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 5 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115587776/

entities.text: Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six (6) months and to pay a fine of Rs.1,000/-, in default, to suffer simple imprisonment for a period of one (1) month.

6. Aggrieved by the said judgment, the revision petitioner/accused preferred an appeal, vide Crl.A.No.48 of 2007, before the Court of learned I Additional Sessions Judge, Nellore and the said appeal was allowed in part by confirming the conviction, but modified and reduced the sentence of imprisonment from six (6) months to three (3) months by confirming the fine imposed by the trial Court.
7. Against the said judgment of the first Appellate Court, the present criminal revision case was preferred by the petitioner/accused.

8. Heard Sri C.Sharan Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner/accused and learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent.
9.

Now the point that arises for determination in this revision is "whether there is any manifest error of law or flagrant miscarriage of justice in the findings recorded by the Trial Court as well first Appellate Court?"
10.

In order to decide the above point, Section 11(4) of the Act has to be keep in mind, which is as follows:
"An article of food seized under sub-section (4) of section 10, unless destroyed under sub-section (4A) of that section, and any adulterant seized under sub-section (6) of that section shall be produced before a magistrate as soon as possible and in any case not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the public analyst.

Provided that if an application is made to the magistrate in this behalf by the person from whom any article of food has been seized, the magistrate shall by order in writing direct the food inspector to produce such article before him within such time as may be specified in the order"
11. It is clear from the above Act, which mandates that any adulterant seized shall be produced before a Magistrate not later than seven days after the receipt of the report of the Public Analyst 12.

In the instant case, there is no oral or documentary evidence placed showing that any report was sent to the learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur from 07.03.2002 to 13.03.2002.

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The evidence of P.W.1 and the complaint were silent regarding the said aspect as mandated under Section 11(4) of the Act.
As per the complaint, the analysis report was said to be filed into the Court on 30.10.2002 along with complaint only.

13. On verification of the record, the learned Assistant Public Prosecutor conceded that nothing is spelt out by the Food Inspector that he sent Ex.P.15-analysis report to the Court within seven days from the date of report.
Hence, it is clear that the complainant-Food Inspector has not followed Section 11(4) of the Act, which is a mandatory provision.

Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 5 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115587776/
2 14.

entities.text: Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The further submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the complainant-Food Inspector failed to take the sample in a clean and dried bottle/container.

In this regard, it is necessary to make a mention of Rule 14 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955, which is as follows:
"14. Manner of sending sample for analysis:-
Samples of food for the purpose of analysis shall be taken in clean dry bottles or jars or in other suitable containers which shall be closed sufficiently tight to prevent leakage, evaporation, or in the case of dry substance, entrance of moisture and shall be carefully sealed"
15.
In this connection, the evidence of P.W.1 is more important.

In the chief examination of P.W.1,
he stated that he had shifted 450 grams of sunflower oil into three clean and dry empty bottles and closed the said bottles and sealed them.

Whereas, in the cross examination, on that particular point,
he stated that "he does not know if the bottles are uncleaned there is possibility of getting resulted as adulterated.

It is true the percentage of cotton seed oil mixed in the sun-flower oil is silent in Ex.P.15 and in the charge sheet".
16.
From the above, it is made clear that the complainant- Food Inspector had not followed the steps while taking the samples and keeping the same in plastic containers.
17. Now, this Court has to consider whether P.W.1 followed Rule 14 of the Rules or not.
As discussed supra, the samples of the food for the purpose of analysis shall be taken in a clean, dry bottles or jars or in any other suitable containers.
But, in this case, P.W.1 categorically admitted that he does not know if the bottles are uncleaned there is possibility of getting resulted as adulterated.
It is a mandatory Rule which has to be followed because, if there is any moisture, that may also give possibility of adulteration.

18. Further the analysis report says that the sample comtain cotton seed oil basing on the Halphen's test, but even the said test is not prescribed under the Clause of 17.15 as well 17.22 in Appendix B of the Act.
As such, Clause 17.15 as well 17.22 in Appendix B of the Act has no application to the case on hand, on which the alleged analyst report was given stating that the sample is adulterated.
The same was not considered by the trial Court as well first appellate Court, which goes to the root of the prosecution case.

19. More so, this Court in Food Inspector v. Gunturu Venkateswara Rao1 observed regarding these facts and held that Section 11 (4) of the Act has to be followed mandatorily as well polythene bag or bottle cannot be called as a container.

entities.text: Food Inspector v. Gunturu Venkateswara Rao1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These two rules were not followed by the complainant-Food Inspector, while seizing and sending the same to the food analysis.

1 2008 (3) ALT (Cri) 238 Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp., on 5 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115587776/
3 20.

entities.text: 2008 (3) ALT (Cri) 238 Gurram Subbarao vs State Of A.P., Rep By Pp
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The trial Court as well first Appellate Court failed to see these mandatory provisions as well fault in the alleged test conducted by the analyst, while coming to the conclusion that the petitioner committed the offence.
Neither the trial Court nor first Appellate Court discussed Section 11(4) of the Act and Rule 14 of the Rules and its compliance.
But, both Section 11(4) of the Act and Rule 14 of the Rules are mandatory to follow as well the alleged test conducted by the analyst not is even prescribed in the said rules.
When those mandatory rules are not followed, invariably it can be said that the prosecution miserably failed to prove the guilt of the petitioner beyond all reasonable doubt.

The Court cannot pass a conviction solely on the remaining evidence and the Court, while finding the guilt, should take care of whether all the mandatory sections and rules were followed by the complainant-Food Inspector or not.
Furthermore, P.W.2, who is said to be mediator, did not support the case of the prosecution and he turned hostile to the prosecution case.
21. In these circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the conviction rendered by the trial Court as confirmed by the first Appellate Court cannot be sustained.

Hence, this Court is of the considered view that the petitioner is able to establish that both the trial Court as well first Appellate Court did not consider Section 11(4) of the Act and Rule 14 of the Rules, which are mandatory.
Thereby, the present criminal revision case is liable to be allowed.

22. In the result, the Criminal Revision Case is allowed conviction and sentence imposed against the petitioner/accused, vide judgment dated 30.04.2007 in C.C.No.558 of 2002 on the file of the Court of learned Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur, which was confirmed with regard to the conviction, but modified the sentence by the judgment dated 18.06.2009 in Crl.A.No.48 of 2007 on the file of the Court of learned I Additional Sessions Judge, Nellore,

entities.text: Additional Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Kovur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: are hereby set aside.
The revision petitioner/accused is acquitted of the charge under Section 16(i)(a)(ii), 7(i) and 2(ia)(b) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act read with Rule 23 and 29 of Food Adulteration Act.
The fine amount paid by the accused, if any, shall be refunded to him.
Interim orders granted earlier if any, stand vacated.

As a sequel, miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
